title: Deprecation Warning Infrastructure
description: Create the shared deprecation warning mechanism used by all command-rename stories (28–35). When a user invokes a deprecated command alias (old name), a warning is printed to stderr before the command executes normally. This keeps the CLI non-breaking while steering users toward the new names.
prerequisiteState: Story 26 complete. Binary is named 'zapi'. No deprecation mechanism exists — there is no standardised way to warn users about renamed commands.
goal: After this story: a static DeprecationHelper.Warn() method exists and can be called from any Command's ExecuteAsync. A Settings base class or marker interface allows an implementing command to flag itself as 'deprecated-invocation'. The approach is documented so all subsequent stories use the same pattern consistently.
scope: Create src/ZapiCli/Commands/DeprecationHelper.cs with a static method: public static void Warn(string oldCommand, string newCommand). The method writes to Console.Error: 'Warning: \'{oldCommand}\' is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Use \'{newCommand}\' instead.' No exit code change — the command still executes normally after the warning.

Decide and document the pattern for how a deprecated registration detects that it is the deprecated alias. The recommended approach: create a marker Settings base class 'DeprecatedCommandSettings : CommandSettings' with a boolean property 'IsDeprecatedAlias { get; init; }' defaulting to false. When registering the deprecated alias, the command class's Settings override sets 'IsDeprecatedAlias = true' via a protected or overridden property — OR — create a separate thin wrapper command class for each deprecated alias that sets the flag. Document which approach is chosen in a file-level comment in DeprecationHelper.cs.

The simpler alternate approach (preferred if the above is complex): Create a second command class for each deprecated alias (e.g., ApiCallCommand next to ApiRequestCommand) that simply sets IsDeprecated = true in its Settings and delegates to the same ExecuteAsync logic. Since Spectre.Console.Cli does not have built-in alias support at the command level, two separate registrations with separate Settings classes is the cleanest solution.
Add a unit test in ZapiCli.Tests confirming that DeprecationHelper.Warn writes to Console.Error and not Console.Out, and that it produces output containing both oldCommand and newCommand strings.
Do NOT implement any actual command renames in this story — only the infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: DeprecationHelper.Warn(string, string) writes a deprecation warning to Console.Error
The deprecation warning message contains the old name and the new name
The deprecation warning does NOT affect the command exit code (still 0 on success)
A unit test verifies stderr output contains both command names
contextForAgent: Spectre.Console.Cli does not support command-level aliases natively (only option aliases via the pipe syntax in CommandOption). To support deprecated command name aliases, register the same (or a thin wrapper) command class twice under two names. The Warn() method is then called at the top of ExecuteAsync when IsDeprecated is set. Read src/ZapiCli/Commands/ to understand existing command class structure before creating the helper. The commands inherit from Command<TSettings> or AsyncCommand<TSettings>.
openItems: Confirm whether commands use Command<T> or AsyncCommand<T> — the ExecuteAsync signature differs. Check AccountLoginCommand as a reference.
